reviews.review:
Very good game. Many other reviews here touch on everything I love and hate about this game.

Having said that; Duoyi Interactive, do you guys need translation help? Some of the descriptions and info could be so much easier to take in with a little QC.

It's pretty fun, but as someone who PRIMARILY enjoys the melee combat of the third character, the bird, Qing Yan, There are a few issues I see shine through, that hopefully get adressed in future updates.

Pros:
- Combat is fluid, feels pretty good, and while the bosses are difficult, they become a lot more consistent with stronger ascension paths and through learning of the mechanics that frankly, don't really get explained well (the lion boss's sand traps and tornadoes cancel each other out.)
- Quite a lot of build variety, sometimes you get ascensions that allow you to run fast, go ham, and tear through the enemies, and sometimes you have to stand further back and attack from long range with snipers and rocket launchers.
- The elemental system, once learned, is incredibly powerful and very useful in the multiplayer setting since you can work with allies to ensure all three main statuses are on enemies at the same time, which can produce some really nice synergistic power.
- Multiple difficulty settings, to allow for newer players that don't want as much of a challenging experience to relax and still get through the game with a smaller amount of combat experience and enemy pattern knowledge, and the pros to test their metal (although good builds still just annihilate the highest difficulty setting at the time of writing).

Cons:

- The big one: The talent system. I'm used to roguelike games that have the main "power" from doing well in the form of unlocks that can be powerful or even gamebreaking. But if you go onto a fully unlocked file and start a new game, you rarely gain any significant power over opening a new file when starting a run, in this game you start with an extra weapon, more health / shield, gold, damage, skill cooldown reduction, crit chance, and crit damage, along with special talents that are extremely powerful on the character that you select, and it feels once you get better that the game is "balanced" with the intent of being fully unlocked, so you're at a disadvantage until you do enough runs to get your stats where they "should" be.
- Like I said early on, I like the melee focused character, Qing Yan. The game has A sword, and it's locked to lightning element, hopefully future updates will give us melee weapons of all 3 elements so a full melee build can be something other than skills and lightning locked.
